events.title: Sad Girlz
about: While preparing for an upcoming swimming trip to Brazil, best friends La Maestra and Paula see their bright futures upended one fateful night. First-time feature director Fernanda Tovar crafts a moving coming-of-age drama in this Berlinale award winner.

events.title: Minotaur
about: Andrey Zvyagintsev’s first feature in a decade, this chilling reimagining of La femme infidèle and Unfaithful masterfully explores the depths of corruption in Vladimir Putin’s Russia through a story of crime and infidelity.

events.title: On Behalf of My Son
about: After losing her son in a tragic accident, a mother travels from one family to another carrying an apology that may be impossible to accept, in Gabriel Martins’s delicate, deeply human meditation on grief and forgiveness.

events.title: Jean-Luc Godard's Early Short Films
about: A glimpse of Jean-Luc Godard in the process of becoming Godard. This program of the director’s first shorts includes Opération béton, All the Boys Are Called Patrick, Une histoire d’eau, and Charlotte et son Jules.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Some Particular Heaven: Ideas of Utopia in the BAMPFA Collection
about: Included with admission.

events.title: A Girl Unknown
about: Born in the wake of China’s controversial one-child policy, six-year-old Juan is suddenly uprooted from her family when her mom becomes pregnant in this achingly poignant coming-of-age story from first-time feature director Zou Jing.

events.title: The Dreamed Adventure
about: A Bulgarian archaeologist investigates the disappearance of a former lover in this absorbing Cannes Film Festival prizewinner. German director Valeska Grisebach worked with a nonprofessional cast to create a slow-burn thriller with the grit of a Western and the scope of Chinatown.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Included with admission.

Graduate students from the Departments of African American and African Diaspora Studies and History of Art offer exhibition tours on selected Wednesdays at 12:15 PM, Sundays at 2 PM, and Free First Thursdays at 1:15 PM.

events.title: Remembering Harun Farocki
about: This is a new restoration of Claudia von Alemann and Reinold E. Thiel’s documentary on the legendary experimental film festival of Knokke, Belgium, featuring political filmmaker Harun Farocki in action. Shown with three short films by Farocki, including Inextinguishable Fire.

events.title: Collaborations with Cairo’s Cimatheque
about: Stefanie Schulte Strathaus has worked closely with Cairo’s Cimatheque – Alternative Film Centre, and she shares two recent restorations completed by the archive, as well as a selection of Egyptian home movies.

events.title: Mosse Lecture–Stefanie Schulte Strathaus: Curating Living Archives
about: Free admission. Tickets available at the admissions desk beginning at 2:30 PM.

Stefanie Schulte Strathaus discusses her work and methodology in the area of curatorial research and archival practice as Artistic Director of Arsenal Filminstitut, Berlin, an institution with deep ties to international film communities.

events.title: Raging Bull
about: 4K Digital Restoration

The biography of boxer Jake LaMotta becomes a visceral meditation on existential suffering. “A fusion of Hollywood genre with personal vision . . . closer to poetry than pulp. Its sculptural weight can only be appreciated on the big screen” (Amy Taubin, Village Voice).

events.title: La maison des bois: Episodes 1–3
about: 4K Digital Restoration
Maurice Pialat’s seven-part series La maison des bois, considered by many to be the director’s best film, is finally available for theatrical exhibition in this new 4K restoration.

about: Included with admission.

Join artist Julia Goodman in creating Wrenching News, a collaborative artwork featured in Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing, through the process of twisting and knotting newspapers according to Hassinger’s specifications.

events.title: White Nights
about: 4K Digital Restoration
Marcello Mastroianni stars in a romantic, sublimely artificial adaptation of a Fyodor Dostoyevsky story about people drifting along crossing, doubling paths.

events.title: Improvisational Screenprinting
about: Space is limited; RSVP required.

Artist Leon Wan leads participants through an experimental and improvisational approach to screenprinting, centering emotion and energy through spontaneous imprints of shape, pattern, and color rather than printing a single fixed image.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Included with admission.

Graduate students from the Departments of African American and African Diaspora Studies and History of Art offer exhibition tours on selected Wednesdays at 12:15 PM, Sundays at 2 PM, and Free First Thursdays at 1:15 PM.

events.title: Shaihu Umar
about: Digital Restoration

Shaihu Umar by Adamu Halilu is an epic story set in northern Nigeria at the end of the nineteenth century. Long thought lost, copies of the film were found in 2016, which led to this restoration by Arsenal Filminstitut.

events.title: The King of Comedy
about: A crazed would-be stand-up comic (Robert De Niro) becomes obsessed with a talk-show host (Jerry Lewis) in Martin Scorsese’s prescient meditation on the American cult of celebrity.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Included with admission.

Graduate students from the Departments of African American and African Diaspora Studies and History of Art offer exhibition tours on selected Wednesdays at 12:15 PM, Sundays at 2 PM, and Free First Thursdays at 1:15 PM.

events.title: Marjorie Keller Films
about: The late Marjorie Keller’s films ranged from social and political critiques to intimate portraits of people who populated her world. Her intricate visual and sound editing is pointed while also being poetically suggestive. On the occasion of a new book about Keller’s films, contributor Steve Anker presents five of her films.

events.title: Breathless
about: 4K Digital Restoration
Jean Seberg and Jean-Paul Belmondo star in the jazzy genre pastiche that launched Jean-Luc Godard’s career and embodied the breathless bravado of the French New Wave.

events.title: La maison des bois: Episodes 1–3
about: 4K Digital Restoration
Maurice Pialat’s seven-part series La maison des bois, considered by many to be the director’s best film, is finally available for theatrical exhibition in this new 4K restoration.

events.title: The Arch
about: 4K Digital Restoration

A Ming dynasty widow, beloved for her grace and kindness, becomes tempted by a visiting soldier in this investigation of propriety, tradition, and repression. This early precursor of the Hong Kong New Wave was praised as “a film of poetic beauty” by Anaïs Nin.

events.title: La maison des bois: Episodes 4–7
about: 4K Digital Restoration
Maurice Pialat’s seven-part series La maison des bois, considered by many to be the director’s best film, is finally available for theatrical exhibition in this new 4K restoration.

events.title: Le petit soldat
about: A disillusioned French counteragent in Geneva becomes embroiled with Algerian separatists, Parisian torturers, and Anna Karina in Jean-Luc Godard’s second film, banned for three years in France.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Included with admission.

Graduate students from the Departments of African American and African Diaspora Studies and History of Art offer exhibition tours on selected Wednesdays at 12:15 PM, Sundays at 2 PM, and Free First Thursdays at 1:15 PM.

events.title: Colorful Youth
about: Digital Restoration

A teen melodrama with a touch of song-and-dance, Colorful Youth is the only film with a contemporary setting starring both Connie Chan Po-chu and Josephine Siao Fong-fong, unequivocally the most popular teen idols in the history of Cantonese cinema.

events.title: After Hours
about: 4K Digital Restoration

A chance encounter with Marcy (Rosanna Arquette) sends hapless office worker Paul (Griffin Dunne) downtown for a date in this zany Kafkaesque comedy set in the apartments, dive bars, diners, clubs, and streets of Soho at night.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Some Particular Heaven: Ideas of Utopia in the BAMPFA Collection
about: Included with admission.

events.title: Our Sister Hedy
about: Four grown sisters navigate a tangle of marriage plots in this charming dramedy. Director Doe Ching “casts the four actresses in roles that fit perfectly like a glove” (Hong Kong Film Archive).

events.title: Celluloid Frontiers: A Missing Can of Film and Stop Genocide
about: Co-sponsored by the Institute for South Asia Studies, UC Berkeley and the Chowdhury Center for Bangladesh Studies, UC Berkeley, and the South Asia Art Initiative at UC Berkeley.

In conjunction with the exhibition Private Frontiers, BAMPFA presents Naeem Mohaiemen’s A Missing Can of Film (2025) and Zahir Raihan’s Stop Genocide (1971)—a film edited in the style of Soviet Realism and Third Cinema during the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War.

events.title: La maison des bois: Episodes 4–7
about: 4K Digital Restoration
Maurice Pialat’s seven-part series La maison des bois, considered by many to be the director’s best film, is finally available for theatrical exhibition in this new 4K restoration.

events.title: A Woman Is a Woman
about: 4K Digital Restoration
“A whimsical celebration of romance, sentiment, musical comedy, color film, the city of Paris and the abundant charms of Anna Karina” (New York Times).

events.title: Performance / Entanglement: Steffani Jemison and Leslie Cuyjet on Maren Hassinger and Senga Nengudi
about: Tickets required. Gallery admission included with ticket purchase.

Artist Steffani Jemison and choreographer Leslie Cuyjet perform a collaborative piece that reflects on the dynamic artistic relationship between Maren Hassinger and Senga Nengudi, the intense intimacy and attunement involved in longstanding artistic collaborations, and the powerful intergenerational legacy of the artists' collective works.

events.title: Vivre sa vie
about: Jean-Luc Godard’s fragmentary portrait of a prostitute makes Anna Karina an object of endless visual fascination. It inspired Rainer Werner Fassbinder to cast Karina in Chinese Roulette. “A film of extraordinary purity” (Manny Farber).

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Included with admission.

Graduate students from the Departments of African American and African Diaspora Studies and History of Art offer exhibition tours on selected Wednesdays at 12:15 PM, Sundays at 2 PM, and Free First Thursdays at 1:15 PM.

events.title: The Valiant Ones
about: BAMPFA Collection
A righteous husband-and-wife swordfighting duo is called to protect China from the machinations of Japanese pirates and corrupt officials in King Hu’s masterly work.

events.title: GoodFellas
about: 4K Digital Restoration

Martin Scorsese’s adaptation of Nicholas Pileggi’s chronicle of real-life Mafia associate Henry Hill, hurtles through some twenty-five years of “family” life, as the riveting Ray Liotta inhabits Hill’s chilling and darkly humorous first-person account.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Included with admission.

Graduate students from the Departments of African American and African Diaspora Studies and History of Art offer exhibition tours on selected Wednesdays at 12:15 PM, Sundays at 2 PM, and Free First Thursdays at 1:15 PM.

events.title: Harun Farocki’s War at a Distance and Videos by Mahmoud Alhaj
about: Harun Farocki’s influential 2003 essay film and Mahmoud Alhaj’s recent videos examine how perception is controlled as a result, or a tool, of war and conflict.

events.title: Curator’s Tour / Anthony Graham on Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Senior Curator Anthony Graham offers a tour of Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing which he co-curated with Chief Curator Margot Norton. Author of the lead exhibition catalogue essay, Graham will explore the evolution of Hassinger's practice through her material experiments in sculpture, her long-standing engagement with movement and performance, and her work with the moving image.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Included with admission.

Graduate students from the Departments of African American and African Diaspora Studies and History of Art offer exhibition tours on selected Wednesdays at 12:15 PM, Sundays at 2 PM, and Free First Thursdays at 1:15 PM.

events.title: Wrenching News Workshops
about: Included with admission.

Join artist Julia Goodman in creating Wrenching News, a collaborative artwork featured in Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing, through the process of twisting and knotting newspapers according to Hassinger’s specifications.

events.title: The Secret
about: Digital Restoration

Loosely based on a real-life double-murder case, Ann Hui’s grisly debut feature traces the labyrinthine investigation by one of the victim’s friends, played by Sylvia Chang. At once procedural and spectral, The Secret “thrives on pure cinematic wizardry” (Faith Everard, Senses of Cinema).

events.title: Mean Streets
about: 4K Digital Restoration

Set during the Feast of San Gennaro in the Italian neighborhood where Martin Scorsese grew up, and populated with characters and situations based on the neighborhood’s inhabitants, Mean Streets is a brilliant distillation of the themes that would define the director’s career.

events.title: Harakiri
about: Tatsuya Nakadai is a penniless samurai who asks a wealthy clan's permission to commit ritual suicide—though that’s not the only killing on his mind. “Probably the best samurai film ever made” (Washington Post).

events.title: Kwaidan
about: 4K Digital Restoration, Director’s Cut

This is Masaki Kobayashi’s atmospheric and visually captivating adaptation of four haunting stories by Lafcadio Hearn. “Each of the exquisitely crafted tales . . . is, in its own right, one of the great ghost stories brought to the screen. Together, they form an exemplar of the anthology horror film” (Village Voice).

events.title: The Sword
about: “With its blend of melodrama, weapons-based action, and wire-fu choreography . . . [The Sword] gets as swept up by the characters’ quieter moments of their muted agony as it does by their physical violence” (Jake Cole, Slant Magazine).

events.title: Mapping Utopias
about: Space is limited; RSVP required.

Educator, anthropologist, and community organizer Isa Prieto leads participants through a discussion and collective mapmaking activity exploring the idea of utopianism and the fragments of utopia that already live in our neighborhoods.

events.title: The Human Condition I: No Greater Love
about: Masaki Kobayashi’s three-part antiwar masterpiece follows the awakening—and disillusionment—of a Japanese soldier (the great Tatsuya Nakadai) during World War II. “Amazingly powerful in its emotional sweep and the depth of its historical insight. . . . Kobayashi’s monumental film can clarify and enrich your understanding of what it is to be alive” (New York Times).

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Some Particular Heaven: Ideas of Utopia in the BAMPFA Collection
about: Included with admission.

events.title: Contempt
about: 4K Digital Restoration
Jean-Luc Godard’s Homeric homage to Fritz Lang, “one of the defining moments of modernist filmmaking” (Film Comment). With Brigitte Bardot, Michel Piccoli, and Jack Palance.
